column1: # VICReg variance + covariance in LATENT SPACE, on the Q02 base. User direction 2026-09-20
# (latent only -- gene space and gene delta explicitly dropped).
# WHY. F-latent7 measured the latent's EFFECTIVE RANK at 32.9 of 512 on Q02 and 24.6 on M03 --
# the representation uses ~5-6% of its dimensions. Our latent MSE already plays VICReg's
# INVARIANCE role; these are the two terms that stop an invariance objective collapsing the
# representation.
# PRE-REGISTERED SPLIT OF EXPECTATION (F-latent7): only 0.6% of dims are dead (std < 0.01), so
# the VARIANCE term has little to fix; the dims are alive but heavily REDUNDANT, so the
# COVARIANCE term is the one with a real target. Expect cov to matter and var not to. If var
# helps more, the reading of the std distribution was wrong.
# WEIGHTS ARE SCALE-MATCHED to Q02's own latent term, which contributes
#     variance  gamma 0.55 (the measured MEDIAN std): term 0.117 -> parity 0.0487
#     variance  gamma 1.00 (the paper's value):       term 0.435 -> parity 0.0131
#     covariance:                                     term 7.05  -> parity 0.00081
# ⚠️ gamma is NOT the paper's 1.0 by default. Measured per-dim std here is ~0.55-0.60, so
# gamma=1 keeps the hinge permanently active and degenerates into "make every dim bigger".
# V07 runs gamma=1.0 deliberately, as the control for that choice.
# TARGETS. delta_z vs z_hat are NOT equivalent: verified they differ 6x in covariance under a
# per-row control (7.66 vs 47.21). F-latent7's probe could not separate them because it fed one
# control per cell line, which makes z_hat a constant shift of delta_z.
# READ AGAINST (test, uncalibrated, 5/5): Q02 0.3783 / mae 0.0225 / ovl@N 0.0774 / disc_l1 0.7029.
# ANCHORS: meanpert 0.1324 · transfer 0.2323 · experimental 0.3722 (mae 0.0257).
# `mae` is an ERROR: LOWER IS BETTER.
# ⚠️ Also re-measure EFFECTIVE RANK on the resulting checkpoints -- that is the direct test of
# whether the term did what it was added for, independent of whether the score moves.
arm
